exact_statement: Determine how large n must be as a function of r >= 2 so that there is an antichain in 2^[n] occupying n-3 distinct ranks and containing at least r members on every occupied rank.
scope_notes: Round five leaves only a change of the H/q leading staircase or bottom recurrence as a local escape interface.
This round asks for the exact linear-in-q slope budget any such one-step switch must satisfy before canonical continuation can coexist with nonnegative surplus.
A slope-budget necessary condition is route evidence only: it neither constructs a legal Macaulay switch nor proves suffix persistence or the public antichain bound.
